questions.q: What did Purdue claim about OxyContin to win FDA approval?
a: That its time-release design would limit addiction by smoothing out highs and lows
That its formula was safer than morphine because it contained no opium
That it would replace surgery painkillers and end illegal drug use
That it worked faster than MS Contin while costing far less to make
questions.why: Lesson 1 explains that Purdue sold the FDA on time-release technology supposedly restricting the highs and lows that drive addiction.

questions.q: Why were Purdue's early addiction figures for OxyContin misleading?
a: They came from controlled hospital tests, not from ordinary patients
They were based on a single clinic with only four patients
They counted only people who had also used heroin
They were collected by Purdue's own sales representatives
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the low addiction rates came from testing in controlled hospital conditions, while the drug was marketed to doctors outside hospitals.

questions.q: What did the short New England Journal of Medicine paragraph about painkillers actually report?
a: Four addictions among about 12,000 patients in a hospital database
Four addictions among 120 patients in a single hospital ward
That OxyContin was safe for all chronic pain patients
That heroin users were switching to prescription pills in large numbers
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes a doctor compiling a hospital database of roughly 12,000 patients and finding only four painkiller addictions.

questions.q: How did daily overdose deaths in the US change between 1999 and 2012?
a: They rose from about 10 a day to about 48
They fell from about 48 a day to about 10
They rose from about 48 a day to about 136
They stayed near 25 a day throughout
questions.why: Lesson 2 notes that overdose deaths averaged about 10 a day in 1999 and about 48 a day by 2012.

questions.q: What did Jo Anna Krohn do after her son died from an OxyContin-related injury?
a: She founded SOLACE to support grieving parents
She sued Purdue and won a public settlement
She opened a clinic for people addicted to painkillers
She campaigned for stricter prescribing laws in her state
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes Krohn starting SOLACE to help parents whose children died of opiates, and it grew to chapters in 16 counties.
